claims.text: Slight temperature and pressure variations alter adsorbate coverage on Ni-, Pd-, and Pt-based catalysts under typical heterogeneous catalytic conditions.
Changes in adsorbate coverage dynamically shift the d-band center of Ni-, Pd-, and Pt-based catalysts.
Dynamic shifts of the d-band center govern catalytic activity and selectivity.
The comparison begins with well-defined, as-prepared, unreacted Ni-, Pd-, and Pt-based catalysts.
Temperature and pressure will be varied while electronic structure is monitored in operando using XAS and XPS.
Temperatures of 300–600 K and pressures of 1–10 atm represent moderate heterogeneous catalytic conditions for the proposed comparison.
Water splitting and hydrocarbon dehydrogenation are representative reaction settings for the proposed study.
Adsorbate-coverage variations induce changes in local oxidation state and active-site symmetry.
Adsorbate-induced d-band-center shifts modify the binding energies of reaction intermediates.
Modification of intermediate binding energies changes the reaction energy profile.
The resulting change in the reaction energy profile enhances catalytic activity and improves selectivity.
A measurable positive shift in the d-band center will produce higher conversion and improved product selectivity relative to baseline.
The baseline consists of catalysts at standard temperature and pressure with fixed adsorbate coverage and corresponding baseline electronic and catalytic properties.
The proposed mechanistic relationship should hold under moderate heterogeneous reaction conditions.
At very high temperature, high pressure, or in unusual reaction environments, factors other than the d-band-center mechanism may dominate.
The d-band-center shift required for a significant performance change is unknown, and other structural parameters may contribute.
Absence of a systematic relationship between measurable d-band-center changes and activity or selectivity changes would falsify the hypothesis.
